in_text_mentions: Furuncles mainly affect areas rich in hair follicles, such as the armpits and the gluteal region, with the formation of abscesses in the hypodermis. Hair follicles are the gateway to S. aureus, favoring its development. It usually presents as an erythematous, painful, and floating nodule, with pustules on the surface and a drainage point. A single or multiple concomitant lesions can be observed (Fig. 10).Figure 10MRSA furunculosis. A healthy 42-year-old patient with several abscesses and furuncles. Positive culture for MRSA with production of Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a human patient explicitly captioned as a carbuncle in insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus. The image visibly shows the classic carbuncle phenotype: an infiltrated erythematous-wine colored plaque with a central ulcerated necrotic core/eschar and purulent drainage, matching the caption and the in-text definition of carbuncle as coalescent furuncles with multiple drainage sinus tracts. Fair/light surrounding skin is visible; no ethnicity or age is stated. No diagrams, controls, or other-disease panels present. [raw subtype: carbuncle]

in_text_mentions: Carbuncle is the coalescence of two or more furuncles in the same locus, with multiple drainage sinus tracts, which tends to extend more deeply into the hypodermis (Fig. 11). Systemic symptoms are usually present and regional lymphadenopathy can be observed. Laboratory findings showed leukocytosis (WBC 14,290/µL; normal 4000–11,000/µL), neutrophilia (94.3%; normal 40–74%), and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP 121 mg/L; normal < 5).

in_text_mentions: A 7-year-old girl with atopic dermatitis was referred to the National Center for Child Health and Development (Tokyo, Japan) for impetigo and recurrent multiple furuncles (furunculosis) (Figure 1). The child had no history of serious infections and no suspected immunodeficiencies. We instructed the patient to maintain skin cleanliness by showering and using moisturizers and to repeatedly treat with oral antimicrobial agents when furuncles manifested. However, the skin lesions relapsed 2–4 weeks after discontinuing the antimicrobial therapy. Culture of the pus from a furuncle identified MSSA (s

ecimens at the initial visit, as well as those (JH62F, JH62M, and JH62B1) from nasal swab specimens of the father, mother, and older brother, were identified as MSSA sequence type (ST) 2233 (Appendix Figure 1). ST2233 belongs to clonal complex (CC) 188, as determined by eBURST analysis of PHYLoViZ version 2.0 web tool (https://www.phyloviz.net). JH62PP2, isolated from the patient’s pus at the follow-up visit, belonged to ST1, and JH62B2, isolated from the younger brother’s nasal swab, ST188; their STs were distinct from ST2233, which was the ST of the suspected strain of household transmission

findings.label: Furuncle with central pustule
findings.evidence: Caption: 'A boil situated in the patient's right temporal region.'; in-text: 'a 1 cm boil on his forehead ... with minimal pus formation'; visual shows an erythematous furuncular nodule with a central pustule.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient. The caption explicitly identifies a boil in the right temporal region and the in-text describes a 1 cm boil with minimal pus formation in a 44-year-old diabetic male, and the article title centers on a temporal boil; the visible lesion is a solitary erythematous furuncular nodule with central pustule/pus, i.e. a classic furuncle (not a multilocular carbuncle). No diagram, control, other disease, or third-party material is present. [raw subtype: furuncle]

panels.figure_caption: A boil situated in the patient's right temporal region.
in_text_mentions: A 44‐year‐old male with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus type 2 on metformin presented to the Emergency Department with a two‐day history of right‐sided chest pain and shortness of breath. Remarkably, the patient had a 1 cm boil on his forehead (Figure 1) with minimal pus formation, which he had noticed a few days earlier. Upon presentation, vital signs indicated hypotension, tachycardia, tachypnea, and fever consistent with sepsis: Blood Pressure 94/53 mmHg, Heart Rate 102 bpm, respiratory rate 26 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98%, temperature 38.2°C.
